**Session Life: The Call Sheet Chronicles**

I sat at my desk, surrounded by dusty recording equipment and scattered papers, as I prepared to scan the call sheet from our recent session with the band, Baby Animals. The sheet, worn and creased, held the secrets of a chaotic recording day. I unfolded it, and my eyes scanned the neatly typed schedule: "10:00 - Start Session."

The clock on the wall read 9:55, and I could feel the excitement building. Our engineer, Mark, was already setting up the microphones, while the band members chatted quietly, sipping their coffee. But as the scheduled start time ticked closer, the room remained quiet.

At 10:15, the call sheet proudly boasted, "All present." I smiled, knowing that our team was finally ready to get started. But little did I know, this was just the beginning of a day filled with unexpected twists and turns.

A handwritten note, scribbled in the margin, caught my eye: "Guest keys L. Matthews arrives 11:30." I raised an eyebrow, wondering who this mysterious guest was and why they were running so late. It wasn't until I reviewed the session tapes that I realized the significance of this note.

In the early 1990s, the Australian music scene was abuzz with the emergence of Baby Animals, a band that would soon capture the hearts of fans and critics alike. With their raw energy, catchy hooks, and sultry vocals, Baby Animals were an instant sensation, joining a wave of female-fronted rock bands that dominated the decade.
